GENERAL SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

2. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. pascal (Pa)

3. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Producers
   D. Primary consumers only

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.

5. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.

10. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole 2.3 Hydrocarbons 3.0 Natural Physical Science 3.1 Thin Lenses 3.2 Newto? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Mole 2.3 Hydrocarbons 3.0 Natural Physical Science 3.1 Thin Lenses 3.2 Newto.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Mole 2.3 Hydrocarbons 3.0 Natural Physical Science 3.1 Thin Lenses 3.2 Newto.

   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole 2.3 Hydrocarbons 3.0 Natural Physical Science 3.1 Thin Lenses 3.2 Newto.

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Newton’s Laws of motion ● Newton’s laws of motion (experimental treatment on ine and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
